A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RISE study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including the new appendices J–K in v4.

before.justification: v2 reports original RISE evaluations on mathematical reasoning, logical reasoning and code generation, alongside ablations, error analyses and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds error distributions in Tables 26–30 and an evaluated SFT baseline in Table 31.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.2, Algorithm 1 and Equations 1–3 retain the same sampling, error injection, filtering, pair construction and adaptive-NLL-augmented DPO procedure. The added SFT procedure serves as a comparator.

E1.justification: All training and evaluation datasets and tasks are retained. The new error analyses use MATH and SVAMP, and the SFT comparison uses GSM8K, MATH, ZebraLogic Cell and HumanEval, all already evaluated in v2.

E2.justification: Appendix K and Table 31 add Qwen2-7B-SFT as an evaluated comparator on four existing benchmarks or metrics. The comparison methods in the retained tables remain unchanged, including GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet despite citation edits.

E3.justification: Appendix K introduces a control trained on the same chosen solutions used by RISE, treating them as supervised targets to examine the training objective. Existing evaluation metrics, decoding settings, dataset splits and RISE training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix J extends the Qwen2/MATH error analysis to Llama-3.1 and Ministral on MATH and three models on SVAMP, testing the taxonomy's applicability. Appendix K adds a supervised-training control. These are focused extensions; existing ablations, sensitivity analyses and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run estimates, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The manual validation of error classification remains 46 correct classifications among 50 samples. New error distributions continue the existing descriptive reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 26–30 add error-type percentages. Table 31 newly reports SFT scores of 87.8, 59.1, 12.48 and 31.1 on GSM8K, MATH, Cell and HumanEval, alongside retained RISE scores of 88.4, 59.9, 23.2 and 47.5. Existing numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The filtering definition and loss formulations in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs relative to the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about subtle-error mitigation, adaptive training stabilization and transfer beyond mathematics. The revised title and new supporting experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix J newly interprets the error distributions as evidence that the taxonomy generalizes across models and datasets. Appendix K contrasts RISE's transfer with SFT's limited generalization. Earlier mechanism explanations, failure discussions and the limitations section remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 newly states that closed-source baselines were accessed through their respective APIs and specifies how chosen RISE solutions become SFT targets. Existing software versions, hyperparameters, evaluation-script references and data-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 removes the Anthropic (2024) reference and the closed-model citations from the baseline paragraph. Appendix K adds a limited positioning contrast with SFT. Section 4's literature discussion and novelty claim remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Subtle Errors Matter' to 'Subtle Errors in Reasoning'. v4 adds acknowledgments, appendices J–K and a short API disclosure, while retaining almost all existing prose and section organization.

P2.justification: v4 adds five error-distribution tables and one SFT comparison table. Table 15 moves alongside Table 16, and nearby text and prompt tables reflow. Existing figures and table designs are retained without substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's Qwen2/MATH-focused diagnosis, Appendix J provides broader support for the error taxonomy. Appendix K's shared-chosen-solution SFT control also strengthens the empirical comparison. These are useful, bounded improvements. The claim that standard SFT fails to generalize exceeds the single-model evidence, and the discussion mentions Puzzle accuracy although Table 31 reports only Cell accuracy; these weaknesses limit the gain.
